balance.argument_a: Young drivers carry the single highest per-vehicle claims rate of the three age classes in the 2019 forecast (Ĉ2,112 vs. Senior's Ĉ2,089 and Middle-aged's Ĉ1,866) -- on a 'which class is worst in isolation' reading, Young is the worst actor. Cutting Young also removes the smallest, least-established piece of Safetylife's book (about 226,600 forecast car-years, versus roughly 647,700 for Senior), meaning far less customer and premium disruption. This matches real actuarial practice: IIHS data shows 16-19 year-old drivers have a fatal crash rate over 3x that of drivers 20+, largely attributed to inexperience (S1) -- a defensible, well-precedented reason to flag the youngest class first.
balance.argument_b: Even though Young's own rate is a hair higher in isolation, Senior carries nearly 3x Young's exposure and the second-highest per-vehicle rate of the three classes. Discontinuing Senior removes about Ĉ1.35 billion of forecast 2019 claims cost (versus only about Ĉ0.48 billion for Young) and produces a LOWER blended claims-cost-per-vehicle for Safetylife's surviving book than discontinuing Young does -- a real, if narrow, edge on exactly the metric Kimuni's 2% profitability promise depends on. Real-world actuarial data also supports treating 65+ as a genuine risk threshold: IIHS attributes older drivers' elevated fatal-crash risk to injury severity and medical complications, not crash frequency (S2) -- a different, equally real reason to flag the class, and one a room defending A has to answer.
balance.margin_basis: Compare the blended (exposure-weighted) 2019 forecast claims cost per vehicle across the two remaining classes under each option: Option A keeps Middle+Senior, Option B keeps Young+Middle. See cases/insurance-actuary/sensitivity_model.py:evaluate() for the exact computation.

modeling_assumptions.assumption: The 2016-2018 quarterly trend (fitted by least-squares regression) continues unchanged into 2019, for every driver-age class.
modeling_assumptions.basis: Standard actuarial trending practice absent any signal of a rate change, new regulation, or underwriting shift for 2019 -- none of which Safetylife has announced.
modeling_assumptions.sensitivity: The answer is sensitive to how far this assumption is trusted; flexed +/-50% in cases/insurance-actuary/sensitivity_model.py (Tier 2 Probe 5).

sensitivity_note: One stated modeling assumption (MA1: linear trend continuation into 2019) is flexed +/-50% by sensitivity_model.py. See QA_REPORT.md for the recorded P5 result.
